key_insight: Relay contact welding can silently compromise student-built emergency-stop circuits despite successful commissioning-time functional tests.
engineering_relevance: Workshop safety assurance should include monitoring sensitive to welded contacts rather than relying solely on initial stop-function checks.
method: Model the circuit as a series safety function degraded by relay contact welding.
Derive conditions under which welded contacts cause an undetected failure on a stop demand.
Simulate a before-after-control-impact estimator across cluster counts and effect sizes.
evidence_signal: The evaluation used 2,000 replications per design cell with 8–32 clusters and 3–8-percentage-point effects, reporting that 54 clusters are needed for 80% power to detect a 5-percentage-point effect.
watch_item: The power estimate depends on the declared variance assumptions; the abstract does not report measured injury outcomes or field validation of integrity monitoring.
paper_title: Functional-Safety-Integrity Degradation of Student-Built Emergency-Stop Circuits in Engineering Technology Education Workshops: A Fault-Injection Evaluation Linking Relay Contact Welding to Operator Injury-Risk Exposure
